title: Nuclei Isolation on Murine DRG for Single Nucleus RNA Sequencing
author: Julia Younis
materials: Prepare lysis, wash, and resuspension buffers. Lysis Buffer (2 mL per sample): Add 10 μL RNase Inhibitor to 2 mL nuclei extraction buffer Wash Buffer (10.59 mL per sample): Add 1.5 mL nuclei extraction buffer to 9 mL chilled 1x PBS Add 40 μL 10% BSA solution Add 50 μL RNase Inhibitor Resuspension Buffer (2 mL per sample) Add 10 μL RNase Inhibitor to 1.8 mL chilled 1x PBS Add 200 μL 10% BSA

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Reagents
steps.instruction: Set up the workstation and prepare necessary materials on ice.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the GentleMACS Dissociator, wait 30 seconds, and select program '4C_nuclei_1' from the favorites folder.

Prepare ice coolers with the following per sample: 1 petri dish, 1 razor blade, 1 C-tube, 1 15mL conical (uncoated), 1 BSA-coated FACS sorting tube, two 30μm cell strainers, and 1 LS separation column.
Coat the FACS sorting tube with 10% BSA solution by pouring it in, swirling, and pouring it out.

steps.title: Anesthetize and Prepare Mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse and sterilize the surgical field.

substeps.instruction: Induce anesthesia via inhalation of 4-5% isoflurane; confirm with a toe pinch.
Fix the mouse on a Styrofoam board using 30-gauge syringes or needles in the paws.
Sterilize the ventral abdominal area with 70% ethanol.

steps.title: Expose Thoracic Cavity and Perfuse
steps.instruction: Perform surgery to access the heart and clear blood from the system.

substeps.instruction: Make a lateral incision across the abdominal skin, then cut down the midline to the thoracic cavity.
Pull back skin flaps to expose the peritoneum and make a lateral incision across the parietal peritoneum to expose the liver and diaphragm.
Slowly inject 5 mL (up to 10 mL if needed) of room temperature 1x PBS into the left ventricle using a 27.5-gauge needle angled towards the aorta; proceed when exiting fluid is clear.
Cut the diaphragm in a crescent shape along the ribs to expose the thoracic cavity.
Snip open the right atrium for exsanguination.
Create a rib cage flap by making two upward cuts on the left and right sides; secure the flap with a hemostat.

steps.title: Isolate Spinal Column
steps.instruction: Expose and remove the relevant section of the spine.

substeps.instruction: Position the mouse dorsal side up; cut and pull back skin to expose the spine and back muscles.
Locate floating ribs at T13 (L1 is directly beneath). To isolate L3-L5 DRGs, cut between L1 and L2, and after L6 (or cut before L3 and after L5 for L4 only).
Trim muscles around the spine with small surgical scissors, ensuring floating ribs remain intact; trim aggressively on the ventral side and leave some muscle on the dorsal side.
Make upward cuts on both sides of the outer ribcage and cut across the top to free the ribs and spine.
Using large surgical scissors, cut from the base of the tail up alongside the spine to separate it from the ilium on both sides, avoiding ribs near the spine.
Remove the tail by cutting at its base.

steps.title: Extract DRGs
steps.instruction: Dissect the spine to isolate the dorsal root ganglia (DRGs).

substeps.instruction: Cut the spine fragment in two along the midline into equal halves.
With the ventral side facing up, remove the front plate of the spine (approx. 1 mm thick) by making vertical cuts to the right and left of the midline.
Pin one half of the spine to a black rubber-bottomed petri dish under a dissection microscope.
Count vertebrae to the target DRG; remove meninges with fine forceps, grab the DRG root, and pull to release the ganglion.
Trim DRG roots as close as possible using small spring scissors.
Remove remaining organs and ventral connective tissues until only muscle remains.
Collect DRGs in chilled artificial cerebral spinal fluid on ice, using one eppendorf tube per sequencing sample.

steps.title: Lysis and Initial Filtration
steps.instruction: Lyse the tissue and perform the first filtration step.

substeps.instruction: Transfer DRGs to a petri dish on ice; use a P200 to remove any artificial cerebral spinal fluid.
Add 200 μL of lysis buffer to DRGs and mince as small as possible with a razor blade.
Wash the razor blade with 800 μL of lysis buffer over the petri dish.
Transfer DRG pieces and lysis buffer to a chilled C-tube using a P1000; wash the petri dish twice with 0.5 mL lysis buffer and transfer to the C-tube.
Pre-wet a 30μm cell strainer with 1x PBS and place it over a 15 mL conical tube.
Transfer the C-tube contents through the strainer into the 15 mL conical tube.
Close the C-tube and tap the bottom to recover remaining sample; wash the plastic blades of the C-tube cap twice with 1 mL wash buffer over the C-tube and filter into the conical.
Centrifuge the 15mL conical at 500G at 4°C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Mechanical Dissociation
steps.instruction: Use the GentleMACS Dissociator to further process the sample.

substeps.instruction: Place the C-tube in the correct GentleMACS Dissociator slot and start the program.
Place a cooler over the C-tube during the run.
Let the program run for 4 minutes, then abort with 1 minute remaining.

steps.title: Nuclei Purification and Washing
steps.instruction: Clean the nuclei sample and remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Pre-wet a new 30 μm cell strainer with 1x PBS and place over a BSA-coated FACS collection tube (remove excess BSA before filtering).
Filter the sample through the strainer; tap the strainer over the 15 mL conical and transfer any remaining sample via pipette.
Add 450 μL of wash buffer to the collection tube and mix by pipetting up and down 10 times (avoid bubbles).
Centrifuge the FACS collection tube at 500G at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant using a P1000 and P200 until ~50 μL remains; resuspend the nuclei pellet in this remaining volume.

steps.title: Nuclei Quantification (First Check)
steps.instruction: Perform a hemocytometer count to check nuclei concentration and morphology.

substeps.instruction: Mix 3 μL of sample with 3 μL trypan blue in a PCR tube and load onto a hemocytometer.
Count nuclei in 16 big squares.
Calculate: Nuclei number x 2 (dilution factor) x 10 = nuclei/μL. Multiply by 450 μL for total count.
Target concentration for loading is 1000-1500 nuclei per μL.

steps.title: Microbead Depletion
steps.instruction: Use anti-nucleus microbeads and a separation column to purify nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 μL anti-nucleus microbeads to the sample; mix slowly up and down 2-3 times with a P1000 (avoid bubbles).
Incubate the sample upright in the 4°C fridge for 15 minutes.
Prepare the LS separation column on a MACS stand with a waste container.
3 minutes before incubation ends: wash the column 3 times with 1 mL wash buffer (total 3 mL), pipetting into the center to avoid drying.
Add 1 mL resuspension buffer to the center of the column, then quickly add and engage the plunger until bubbles appear.
Add 2 mL wash buffer to the sample and mix slowly 2-3 times with a P1000.
Add 1 mL wash buffer to the column and let flow through.
Add the sample to the center of the column and let flow through.
Place the coated/washed FACS collection tube under the column; transfer both to ice.
Wash the sample tube walls with 1 mL wash buffer and transfer contents to the column.

steps.title: Final Wash and Concentration
steps.instruction: Perform final cleaning and adjust nuclei concentration for loading.

substeps.instruction: Wash the sample by adding 500 μL resuspension buffer, mixing 3-4 times with a P1000, then centrifuging at 500G at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Calculate the volume needed to achieve 1000-1500 nuclei per μL; remove supernatant until this volume remains and resuspend the nuclei.

steps.title: Final Quality Control
steps.instruction: Perform a final count and morphology check before sample loading.

substeps.instruction: Mix 1 μL of sample with 5 μL trypan blue in a PCR tube and load onto a hemocytometer.
Count nuclei in 16 big squares.
Calculate: Nuclei number x 5 (dilution factor) x 10 = nuclei/μL. Multiply by the resuspension volume for total count.
If nuclei are intact with minimal debris at the target concentration, proceed to sample loading. Provide the remaining 500 μL of resuspension buffer to the core.
